summary: The note is a news-style article about the Cyberterritories, an alliance of digital hubs that declared sovereignty from traditional nation-states beginning in early September 2023. It covers their proposed blockchain and AI governance, merit-based digital citizenship and contentious digital visas, their economic weight, cybersecurity plans, and mixed reactions from governments and international bodies. It closes by raising questions about cultural identity, citizenship and the future of the internet.
one_line: News story on the Cyberterritories, an alliance of digital hubs declaring sovereignty in September 2023, and the debate over digital citizenship and governance.
key_facts: On the morning of September 5, 2023, an alliance of digital hubs including Silicon Sanctuary, Netfront Nexus, and Datahaven Delta issued a joint statement declaring sovereignty.
The declaration was signed by self-appointed digital leaders including Evan Turing of Silicon Sanctuary and Rei Nakamoto of Netfront Nexus.
The Cyberterritories intend to form an independent sovereign state free from the jurisdiction of any traditional nation-state.
The alliance's governance model relies on blockchain technologies and advanced AI to administer its systems.
Digital citizenship under the preliminary governance charter will be merit-based and tied to contributions to the digital economy and society, with specifics not yet settled.
One contentious proposal is digital visas for accessing different corners of the internet; critics fear an elitist system and 'cyber-ghettos'.
The Cyberterritories' combined virtual GDP is rumored to surpass even some physical nations, with cryptocurrencies and NFTs as common currencies.
Jessica Morphel of Datahaven Delta stressed creating a sustainable and inclusive digital economy; plans for cyber taxation, public digital services, and virtual infrastructure are under development.
The Cyberterritories pooled resources into a joint cyber defense initiative, though experts doubt it can withstand concerted nation-state attacks.
Leaked documents from Silicon Sanctuary's security division reveal plans for an 'uncharted digital armor' to safeguard its digital borders.
World governments responded in mixed ways, with some rejecting the sovereignty claim and others cautiously engaging.
The United Nations and the International Court of Justice face the challenge of integrating digital entities into a world system built around physical lands.
The Cyberterritories' flagship virtual reality experience is called Metaspace.
